title: The Invoices card counts a billable invoice with a no-charge line once
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Open the dashboard for today and note the Invoices card and the Sales card.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, invoiced today, billable, invoiced after the figures were noted, with line 1 at $240.00 and line 2 marked No Charge under Goodwill.
custom_steps:
1. Open the dashboard.
  2. Set its range to today.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The dashboard opens.

Step 2:

  • "Total invoices in range" is the noted count plus 1: work order 1 counts once.
  • Sales is the noted figure plus $240.00, line 1's amount; line 2 adds $0.00.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11766 (Story 9, Reports, dashboard and exports)

  • S9-R1: “Sales, Sales By Customer, Sales By Representative and Advisor Analysis leave whole internal and no-charge work orders out of every number, with no filter and no option to include them. On a billable work order they leave every no-charge line out of labor revenue, parts revenue, labor cost, parts cost, invoiced hours and worked hours, the way a declined line is left out today: the invoice financial snapshot captures the no-charge lines as excluded, and the per-statement queries carry the same condition. The work order itself stays in with its billable amounts. Every dashboard card and ranking (Sales, Sales by Customer, Top Customers with its invoice count, At-Risk Customers, Billing, and the Invoices card, "Total invoices in range") does the same. The dashboard Tech Efficiency card follows the Technician Efficiency report's default (Show all, S9-R3), so the card and the report give the same hours for a technician.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
